text:
maria: RFC draft up: https://rwd-infer.internal/rfcs/sdklib-streaming-shape — asking for prioritization input. goal is to finalize acceptance criteria + launch gating by EOW. quick context: product wants a streaming-first JS/Python SDK that matches hosted API ergonomics and adds resilient reconnects + backoff.

jonathan: skimmed. big question: do we ship a minimal ergonomic surface first (sync/async iterator + simple callbacks) and iterate on advanced reconnects, or land full-on resume semantics in v1?

sasha: leaning minimal v1 + beta customers. shipping full resume (server-side resume tokens) is more product work and might delay. but we need basic reconnect with idempotency tokens at min.

liam: engineering constraints: runtime has no native resume token support yet. we can implement client-side buffering + replay with idempotency, but result deduping is tricky for partial tokens. timeline for native support ~6 weeks.

priyanka: from PLG/customer side — we have 2 customers asking specifically for resume-on-interrupt (long-lived agents). if we punt, they may churn. proposal: v1 = ergonomic streaming + robust reconnect/backoff (best-effort resume via idempotency), v1.1 = resume tokens + strict exactly-once semantics.

maria: suggested acceptance criteria for v1 (draft):
- SDK exposes streaming API in both JS and Python with the same developer ergonomics (async iterator + on('data') hook).
- Behavior on transient disconnect: automatic reconnect with exponential backoff + jitter, and client attempts to resume from last emitted token if server supports; otherwise reuse idempotency to avoid duplicates.
- Default backoff: base=200ms, max=10s, max_attempts=5. configurable.
- No accidental memory growth across long-lived streams (heap stable under 24h of synthetic load).
- Telemetry: automatic event for stream_disconnect, reconnect_attempt, resume_success/fail.
- Tests: integration test that simulates network drop and asserts at-least-once vs dedup policy.

jonathan: add latencies SLO: p99 end-to-end for single-client streaming server < 150ms under typical load? maybe per-token latency metric instead. also a cost estimate for always-on sockets.

sasha: acceptance criteria note: define exact semantics for partial responses (server may send partial JSON). SDK must provide framing helpers and a stable 'chunk to message' API. include edge case for truncated utf-8 sequences.

liam: edge cases list I care about:
- server returns HTTP 200 then stream ends mid-message (partial JSON)
- network partition + rebind to new server with different model version
- idempotency token collisions across retries
- client cancel while reconnect in-flight
- proxy/timeouts closing idle sockets

priyanka: launch gating (proposed):
- internal dogfood: 2 weeks minimal usage in console + example app.
- external beta: onboard 3 customers, >=1 month usage, no data-loss incidents.
- telemetry thresholds: stream_disconnect rate <1% per request and reconnect_success >95% within 3 attempts.
- docs & quickstarts for both JS and Python + migration guide for non-streaming users.

maria: implementation plan sketch:
1) API design PR: expose Stream object with async iterator + events and small config object { backoff: {base, max, attempts}, idempotency_key }
2) runtime integration: add socket management + client-side buffered cursor handling
3) tests + harness: flaky-network simulator + perf runs
4) docs & example apps
5) beta rollout + metrics watch

priyanka: acceptance criteria for API ergonomics (developer-facing):
- two-line example to read streaming tokens in JS/Python
- clear cancel semantics for users (cancel() returns promise resolves when teardown completes)
- minimal cognitive load: prefer 'for await (const chunk of resp.stream())' over callback chains

jonathan: about retries/backoff: we should use standard exponential backoff with full jitter (per AWS guidance). default attempts 5 but SDK must expose a hook to plug custom strategy. also document behavior when non-idempotent operations are retried — show examples and recommend idempotency usage.

sasha: small API sketch (from the RFC):
```js
const s = client.stream({model: 'gptx-stream', idempotency_key: 'abc-123'});
for await (const part of s) {
  // part.text or part.delta tokens
}
await s.cancel();
```

liam: perf gating: must support 200 concurrent streams on medium tier instance with <5% increase in p50 token latency. include memory/FD usage budget.

maria: who volunteers to own the API PR? I can coordinate product requirements. need eng lead + devex docs owner.

liam: I can lead the runtime changes + perf tests.

jonathan: i'll take the SDK API PR + the JS impl. sasha will help with Python. priyanka can validate customer requirements and run beta onboarding.

priyanka: timeline ask: can we aim for feature freeze in 3 weeks and begin dogfood week 4?

liam: tight but doable if we scope v1 minimal. need to drop server-side resume for v1 to hit that.

maria: consensus check — ship v1 (ergonomic streaming + reconnect/backoff + telemetry + docs) in 4 weeks, ship resume tokens in v1.1. thumbs? :thumbsup:

jonathan: :thumbsup:

sasha: :thumbsup:

priyanka: :thumbsup: on the plan if we get commitment from runtime and SDK owners.

deploy-bot: scheduled ci build triggered for rfc/sdklib-streaming-shape (#432)

maria: OK — I'll land the API PR draft today and tag owners for reviews. Thanks everyone, will post a shorter checklist tomorrow.
